findings.reason: the plan should extend that existing closability predicate (add unresolved-followup / unset-impl / uncollapsed-section conditions) rather than build a parallel gate.
findings.text: §3.5 proposes a close-sprint refusal gate, but `_close_sprint_with_carry_forward` already makes a sprint closable only when every non-terminal item is held by a `held` blocker, else raising ProjectStateError naming the item, using a journal and carry-forward

findings.reason: M3's remaining work is scheduling the existing pass, not building it; the plan's "still pending" line would have an implementer rebuild a landed mechanism.
findings.text: §3.3 states the age-based archive sweep is pending while `reckon/archive.py (run_archive_pass/find_archive_candidates)` and the `reckon archive` CLI already apply exactly the quarterly-style pass over done/superseded docs older than a threshold

findings.reason: if the diet is to have teeth the honest change is extending the existing refusal; a prompt in a skill is the shallow form and adds surface with no enforcement.
findings.text: §3.4's diet is a pre-flight question in the `reckon-create` skill, layered over the existing write-time refusal `unwired_plan_finding`/`_unwired_plan_refusal` that already blocks a new plan declaring no wire

findings.reason: the plan should state the write-time guard consumes the doccheck predicates so the reject/warn severities cannot diverge from the audit's.
findings.text: §3.1's write-time predicates (impl set on ship; landed card present; research-doc closure) restate audit-side checks already owned by `reckon/doccheck.py` — MISSING_IMPL at line 577, landed-card class `_LANDED_SECTION_CLASS` at line 116 — without naming that writes must reuse those predicates

findings.reason: with cli_options at 317 the section must account for the surface it adds; the audit and archive commands landed as new options without any retirement argument.
findings.text: §3.2 and §3.3 add to cli_options (the `audit` and `archive` commands and their options) and neither section, and the rest of §3, names a CLI option or command it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan proposes no new module, and the lifecycle predicates it would add already live in non-shallow owners (`reckon/lifecycle.py` derived state, `reckon/doccheck.py` audit checks), so nothing is spread across a family of shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3.5 would fork sprint closability that `_close_sprint_with_carry_forward` (`reckon/project_state.py:2198`) already enforces.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §3.2–§3.3 add the `audit` and `archive` command options to cli_options and no section names what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3.3 (line 86) declares the archive sweep "still pending" and §3.5 (line 94) proposes a new sprint-close gate, without citing that both mechanisms already exist in the repo it would extend.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3.4 (line 90) adds a skill-level pre-flight question over the existing write-time plan-creation refusal `unwired_plan_finding` (`reckon/doccheck.py:863`) without saying why that check cannot carry the diet.
